_provenance: Defaults are DISCLOSED ASSUMPTIONS, not issuer facts. Each basis names its source and says what it assumes. Owner state overrides any entry per programId; see docs/plans/2026-08-20-catalogue-scalability-program-design.md §3.1.
_method: One rule, applied uniformly, so the numbers mean the same thing on every card. centsPerPoint is the best POSTED FIXED conversion the program publishes — a rate, never a forecast of what a redemption might be worth. floorCentsPerPoint is the rate obtainable with nothing but the card: an unconditional statement credit or cash-out, no qualifying purchase and no second account. It is OMITTED where the program has no cash redemption at all, because Scorer falls back to centsPerPoint and a fabricated floor would pass an assumption off as a guarantee. aspirationalCentsPerPoint carries a published benchmark ONLY where the benchmark exceeds the ranked value; it is a ceiling for disclosing upside breakevens and is never used for ranking. Every programId the catalogue declares is valued here, so CatalogueIntegrityTests.knownUnvaluedPrograms is empty and its ratchet is set to zero.

cashback.basis: A dollar of cash back is a dollar. The only entry in this file that is an issuer fact rather than an assumption.

amexMembershipRewards.basis: Ranked at the guaranteed cash floor — 1.0¢ is Amex Canada's statement-credit rate, which is an issuer fact. Anything above it is a forecast of redemption behaviour and is not assumed here. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 2.2 is the published Canadian transfer-partner benchmark (Prince of Travel, 2026-07-29) and is used ONLY as the plausibility ceiling for disclosing upside breakevens, never for ranking.

marriottBonvoy.basis: ASSUMPTION: 0.8¢ per point on hotel award nights, range 0.6–1.0¢ across property tiers. Bonvoy has no cash-out floor, so there is no issuer fact to anchor to; an owner who redeems differently should override this.

mbnaRewards.basis: 1.0¢ on the travel-redemption schedule. floorCentsPerPoint 0.833333 is the guaranteed cash-back rate (100 points = $0.83), an issuer fact; the 1.0¢ above it assumes travel redemption.

ctMoney.basis: Face value is 1 CT Money = $1.00 at Canadian Tire, an issuer fact. ASSUMPTION: a 0.95 usability factor, applied by default, because CT Money spends only in one retailer's stores and a dollar locked to one merchant is not a dollar. Set usabilityFactorApplied false to value it at face.

cro.basis: CRO is paid as a crypto asset, so its CAD value is only fixed at the moment it is sold. faceValueFactorIfAutoSold 1.0 applies when cardState.croHandling is autoSell — sold on receipt, so face value is realised. ASSUMPTION: 0.8 when held, a haircut for price risk between earning and selling. This is a risk discount, not a price forecast.

scenePlus.basis: Scotiabank posts a fixed 100 points = $1 for Scene+ Travel, Empire-banner groceries and Cineplex, so 1.0¢ is a published rate rather than a forecast (Scotiabank Scene+ points and rewards calculator, checked 2026-08-20). floorCentsPerPoint 0.666667 is the cash-out: Points for Credit starts at 3,000 points for a $20 statement credit (Ratehub, checked 2026-08-20). Prince of Travel (Q2 2026) and Milesopedia (2026-01-01) both benchmark Scene+ at 1.0¢, so there is no upside band to disclose. ASSUMPTION: that the owner redeems at the posted rate rather than taking the credit — one who always takes the credit should override centsPerPoint to the floor.

aeroplan.basis: Aeroplan has NO cash-out and posts no fixed conversion — flight rewards are dynamically priced — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented, and the floor band falls back to the ranked value. Ranked at 1.0¢ by transfer parity: Amex Membership Rewards converts to Aeroplan 1:1 and is ranked in this file at 1.0¢, so valuing Aeroplan above that would make one point worth more after a free transfer than before it. 1.0¢ is independently the rate Air Canada gift cards clear at in the Aeroplan eStore, the program's best fixed-value redemption; other gift cards run about 0.7¢ (Ratehub, checked 2026-08-20). aspirationalCentsPerPoint 2.0 is the published benchmark (Prince of Travel Q2 2026, as of 2026-05-01; Milesopedia agrees at 2.0¢) and is the plausibility ceiling for disclosing upside breakevens, never for ranking. Raise centsPerPoint only from a realised rate the owner has actually achieved.

rbcAvion.basis: 0.58¢ is the one posted rate true for BOTH currencies this programId covers, which is the only reason a single number is defensible. rbc-avion-visa-infinite earns Avion Elite points — statement credit 0.58¢, flexible travel credit 1.0¢, Air Travel Redemption Schedule up to about 2.3¢ — while rbc-ion-plus-visa earns Avion Premium points, whose only fixed redemption is a travel credit at 0.58¢ and which cannot transfer to airlines at all (Prince of Travel, checked 2026-08-20). KNOWN DEFECT: one programId, two currencies that differ by ~1.7×. An Avion Elite owner who takes the 1.0¢ travel credit should override, but the override is per programId, so doing that also over-values the ION+ card. Splitting the programId is the real fix. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 2.0 is the published Elite-transfer benchmark (Prince of Travel Q2 2026, as of 2026-05-01; Milesopedia 2026-01-01 says 1.6¢) and is a disclosure ceiling only.

tdRewards.basis: 0.5¢ is TD's posted rate — 200 TD Points = $1 booked through Expedia for TD — and the program's best fixed-value redemption. floorCentsPerPoint 0.25 is the unconditional cash-out: 400 points = $1 as a statement credit, the same rate gift cards clear at (Ratehub, checked 2026-08-20). Prince of Travel (Q2 2026) and Milesopedia (2026-01-01) both benchmark TD Rewards at 0.5¢, so there is no upside band to disclose. Booking travel any other way is worth less, not more: the first $1,200 of a self-booked trip clears at 250 points = $1.

bmoRewards.basis: 0.666667¢ is BMO's posted rate, reachable two independent ways: 150 points = $1 applied to a travel purchase through Pay with Points, and 15,000 points = $100 cashed into a BMO investment account (Prince of Travel, checked 2026-08-20). floorCentsPerPoint 0.333333 is the unconditional cash-out — 15,000 points = $50 as a statement credit — which needs neither a qualifying travel purchase nor a second BMO account. Prince of Travel benchmarks 0.7¢ and Milesopedia 0.67¢, both at or below the ranked value, so no upside band is disclosed. Gift cards and merchandise sit between the two at roughly 0.54–0.56¢.

aventura.basis: 1.0¢ is CIBC's posted rate — 100 Aventura points = $1 through the CIBC Rewards Travel Centre, or via Shopping with Points applied to a travel charge already on the card. floorCentsPerPoint 0.625 is the cash-out: a minimum 4,000 points for a $25 statement credit (Frugal Flyer, checked 2026-08-20). No aspirational band is set even though the Aventura Airline Rewards Chart can exceed 2¢ on some itineraries, because that value depends on the itinerary rather than on a posted rate; Prince of Travel's whole-program benchmark is 1.0¢, the value ranked here (Milesopedia says 1.2¢).

nbcRewards.basis: 1.0¢ is National Bank's posted rate: 10,000 à la carte points = $100 booked through the À la carte travel agency. floorCentsPerPoint 0.4 is the unconditional cash-out — a statement credit against any purchase, the program's worst posted rate (Frugal Flyer and Money We Have agree, checked 2026-08-20). The spread here is unusually wide and worth seeing: a credit against travel the owner booked themselves, and an RRSP/TFSA contribution, both clear 12,000 points = $100, or 0.833¢. Milesopedia benchmarks the program at 0.9¢, below the ranked value, so no upside band is disclosed; an owner who only ever takes the plain statement credit should override centsPerPoint to 0.4.

pcOptimum.basis: 0.1¢ is the program's only rate and it is fixed: 10,000 PC Optimum points = $10 off a purchase, redeemable in 10,000-point increments at Loblaw-family grocers, Shoppers Drug Mart/Pharmaprix, Joe Fresh and Esso (PC Financial; Milesopedia agrees at 0.1¢, checked 2026-08-20). There is no cash-out, so floorCentsPerPoint is absent and the floor band falls back to this same rate — honest here, because the rate does not vary. ASSUMPTION: that $1 of Loblaw-family credit is worth $1 to the owner. That is the same store-lock question CT Money carries a 0.95 usability factor for; the points model has no such factor, so an owner who rarely shops those banners should override centsPerPoint downward.

westJetPoints.basis: 1.0¢ is WestJet's posted rate: 100 WestJet points = C$1 off base fare, carrier surcharges, bags and seats (westjet.com, checked 2026-08-20). The catalogue's earn figures are WestJet POINTS, not the retired WestJet dollars — the program converted on 2025-04-30 — which is what makes this unit sane: 1.5 points per dollar × 1.0¢ reproduces the card's marketed 1.5% return, and RBC's own product page states the earn as 1.5 and 2 points per dollar. Taxes and fees redeem worse, at 105–115 points per $1. There is no cash-out, so floorCentsPerPoint is absent and the floor band falls back to this rate. ASSUMPTION: that the owner flies WestJet; the points buy nothing else at this rate.

amazonRewards.basis: 1.0¢ is the posted rate and the only one: 100 points = $1, redeemed as an Amazon.ca gift card loaded to the owner's account (MBNA, checked 2026-08-20). It is also the value that reconciles the catalogue's earn figures with MBNA's own marketing — 1 point per dollar is advertised as 1% back, 2.5 points per dollar as 2.5% — so any other number would contradict the earn data this file is scored against. There is no statement credit and no cash-out, so floorCentsPerPoint is absent and the floor band falls back to this rate. ASSUMPTION: that $1 of Amazon.ca credit is worth $1 to the owner; one who does not shop Amazon should override centsPerPoint downward.

aaAdvantage.basis: AAdvantage has NO cash-out and posts no fixed conversion for award flights — awards are dynamically priced — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Ranked at 1.0¢ by transfer parity: Citi ThankYou Rewards converts to AAdvantage 1:1, so valuing AAdvantage above the 1.0¢ baseline bank currency would make one point worth more after a free transfer than before it. The only fixed posted conversion is retail gift cards at ~0.7¢ (aadvantagegiftcards.com, checked 2026-08-27). aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.4 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy and Frequent Miler, checked 2026-08-27) and is the plausibility ceiling for disclosing upside breakevens, never for ranking.

atmosRewards.basis: Atmos Rewards (the unified Alaska/Hawaiian programme) has NO cash-out and posts no fixed conversion — award flights follow distance-based partner bands and dynamic own-metal pricing, and the legacy 1.0¢ 'Money & Miles' cash-offset option was retired in August 2024 — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Ranked at 1.0¢ by transfer parity: transferable partner points convert 1:1, so valuing Atmos above 1.0¢ would make one point worth more after a free transfer than before it. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.5 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy, August 2026; Frequent Miler 1.45¢) and serves solely as the plausibility ceiling for disclosing upside breakevens, never for ranking.

avios.basis: Avios (the shared IAG currency across British Airways, Aer Lingus, Iberia, Qatar, and Finnair) has NO unconditional cash-out on North American credit cards — Chase and RBC cards deposit into frequent flyer accounts with no statement credit floor — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Ranked at 1.0¢ by transfer parity: Amex MR (US and CA), Chase UR, Capital One, and Citi ThankYou all transfer to Avios 1:1, so valuing Avios above 1.0¢ would make one point worth more after a free transfer than before it. Part Payment with Avios on cash flights yields a variable 0.6–1.1¢. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.5 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy, August 2026; Prince of Travel 1.5¢) and is the disclosure ceiling only.

cathayAsiaMiles.basis: Asia Miles has NO cash-out and posts no fixed conversion — standard flight awards follow distance-based zones, while Miles Plus Cash dynamically prices at sub-cent rates — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Ranked at 1.0¢ by transfer parity: Capital One, Citi ThankYou, and RBC Avion all transfer to Asia Miles 1:1, so valuing Asia Miles above 1.0¢ would make one point worth more after a free transfer than before it. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.3 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy and Prince of Travel, August 2026) and is used solely as a plausibility ceiling for upside breakevens, never for ranking.

deltaSkyMiles.basis: 1.0¢ is Delta's posted fixed rate for 'Pay with Miles' — 5,000 miles = $50 off base fare on delta.com — available to all Delta SkyMiles American Express cardholders in this catalogue. Award flights are otherwise dynamically priced. There is NO unconditional cash-out or statement credit against general spend, so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Transfer parity with Amex Membership Rewards (1:1 transfer) independently reinforces the 1.0¢ ceiling. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.2 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy and NerdWallet, August 2026) and serves as the plausibility ceiling for disclosing upside breakevens, never for ranking.

disneyRewards.basis: Face value is 1 Disney Rewards Dollar = $1.00 USD at Disney parks, Disney Cruise Line, DisneyStore.com, and Disney entertainment (Chase and Disney Rewards terms, checked 2026-08-27). This is a store-locked dollar reward, not a points currency. Premier and Inspire cardholders can also redeem 1:1 as a statement credit against airline ticket purchases via Pay Yourself Back. ASSUMPTION: a 0.95 usability factor, applied by default, because Disney Rewards Dollars are locked to Disney-ecosystem spending (or qualified airline tickets) and a merchant-locked dollar is not cash. Set usabilityFactorApplied false to value it at face.

amexMembershipRewardsUs.basis: 1.0¢ on flights booked through Amex Travel. floorCentsPerPoint 0.6 is the standard statement credit cash-out (1.1¢ with Charles Schwab Platinum). aspirationalCentsPerPoint 2.0 is the published transfer benchmark (The Points Guy, August 2026).

chaseUltimateRewards.basis: 1.0¢ is Chase's posted unconditional cash-back and statement-credit rate (100 points = $1.00 USD), an issuer fact. Sapphire Preferred boosts travel redemption to 1.25¢, and Sapphire Reserve to 1.5¢. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 2.0 is the published transfer benchmark (The Points Guy, August 2026).

citiThankYou.basis: 1.0¢ is Citi's posted cash-back rate (100 ThankYou points = $1.00 USD direct deposit or statement credit). aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.8 is the published transfer-partner benchmark.

hiltonHonors.basis: 0.5¢ is the posted fixed conversion rate for Amazon Shop with Points (500 Hilton Honors points = $2.50 off Amazon.com purchases), available directly to cardholders without hotel bookings. 0.5¢ also satisfies transfer parity: Amex Membership Rewards transfers 1:2 to Hilton Honors, so at 1.0¢ Amex MR baseline, valuing Hilton above 0.5¢ would make points worth more after transfer. Hotel award nights are dynamically priced. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 0.6 is the published third-party benchmark (The Points Guy, August 2026; NerdWallet 0.5¢) and serves solely as a disclosure ceiling.

emiratesSkywards.basis: Emirates Skywards has NO cash-out and posts no fixed conversion — Classic Rewards and Cash+Miles dynamically price — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Ranked at 1.0¢ by transfer parity: Amex MR, Chase UR, Citi ThankYou, and Capital One all transfer to Emirates Skywards 1:1, so ranking above 1.0¢ would make one point worth more after a free transfer than before it. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.2 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy and Frequent Miler, August 2026) for upside disclosures only.

frontierMiles.basis: Frontier Miles has NO cash-out and posts dynamic award flight pricing with fixed redemption fee tiers — so floorCentsPerPoint is deliberately absent rather than invented. Ranked at 1.0¢ by award baseline value. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 1.1 is the published benchmark (NerdWallet and The Points Guy, August 2026) and is used only as a disclosure ceiling.

choicePrivileges.basis: 0.6¢ is the median value for standard Choice Hotels free night award stays (Choice Hotels award chart tiers 6,000–35,000 points per night). Ranked at 0.6¢ in alignment with transfer parity: Citi ThankYou transfers 1:2 to Choice Privileges, placing Choice points at ~0.5–0.6¢ relative to Citi's 1.0¢ cash floor. There is NO unconditional cash-out, so floorCentsPerPoint is absent. aspirationalCentsPerPoint 0.8 is the published benchmark (The Points Guy and Frequent Miler, August 2026).

costcoCashRewardsCa.basis: Face value is 1 CAD = $1.00 CAD issued annually as a Cash Back Gift Certificate for redemption at Canadian Costco warehouses. ASSUMPTION: a 0.95 usability factor is applied by default because the reward is locked to Canadian Costco warehouse registers and issued only once per year in January. Set usabilityFactorApplied false to value at 1.0 face.

costcoCashRewardsUs.basis: Face value is 1 USD = $1.00 USD issued annually in February as a Costco Cash Reward certificate redeemable for merchandise or cash at US Costco warehouses. ASSUMPTION: a 0.95 usability factor is applied by default because the reward is distributed annually and restricted to US Costco locations. Set usabilityFactorApplied false to value at 1.0 face.

amazonRewardsUs.basis: 1.0¢ is the posted fixed conversion: 100 points = $1.00 USD on Amazon.com checkout or as a direct cash back / statement credit via Chase.com. floorCentsPerPoint 1.0 is an issuer fact because cardholders can unconditionally cash out into bank accounts or statement credits with no penalty.

noRewards.basis: Not an assumption. The card earns nothing, so its reward currency is worth nothing — the one valuation in this file that is a fact rather than a disclosed estimate.

discoverCashback.basis: Discover Cashback is cash. 1 USD cashback = $1.00 USD.

bofaPreferredRewards.basis: Bank of America cash rewards deposit 1:1 into eligible BofA accounts.
